author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Minnesota Twins center fielder Byron Buxton will miss the rest of the season and undergo arthroscopic surgery on his right hip September 18, the team announced Friday. Buxton has been dealing with a hip impingement that placed him on the injured list three times this season. He last appeared for Minnesota on August 25.

Manager Derek Shelton told reporters that Buxton is expected to recover before the start of the 2027 season. The 32-year-old played 93 games this year, batting .254 with 25 home runs and 46 runs batted in. He also made the American League All-Star team for the second consecutive season and the third time in his career.

Durability has repeatedly shaped Buxton's career. He has reached 100 games in only three of his 12 major-league seasons, including a career-high 140 in 2017. Entering Friday, the Twins were 69-77 and 4 1/2 games behind Cleveland for the American League's third wild-card position. The surgery removes a key bat and defender from Minnesota's late playoff push, but the club's timetable prioritizes a full recovery for next spring.
dek: The Twins center fielder will undergo arthroscopic right-hip surgery September 18 after three injured-list stints this season.
headline: Twins' Byron Buxton set for season-ending hip surgery
